messages.text:
I just received my Hammer Miner BC04 (order number: Shop····) and I
wanted to try out your guys' OS for it, but I'm having issues getting it to
flash properly. I keep getting this error: [image: image.png]

I've tried with a few different cables and 2 different Windows devices and
all of them have led to this same error. Is there something I'm doing
wrong? Here is the installation log: [image: image.png]

I've tried to follow the instructions pushing the buttons as well, but I'm
not entirely sure I am doing it right (the buttons aren't labeled very well
on the microcontroller)
Searched the web · esptool "Invalid head of packet (0x45)" ESP32-S3 web flasher

Hi,

Thanks for sending the screenshot and the log, that pair tells me almost exactly what is happening. The log shows the flasher talking to the chip fine: it identifies an ESP32-S3 (QFN56, rev v0.2), reads the MAC and uploads the stub, so your cable and both PCs are good. The failure comes right after that, and the 0x45 is the giveaway.
0x45 is the ASCII "E" of the chip's own boot banner "ESP-ROM:esp32..." arriving where the flasher expected a reply packet
. In plain terms the chip dropped out of download mode and rebooted into normal firmware mid-flash, so the tool is reading boot text instead of answers. That is why changing cables and PCs made no difference: it is not a bad cable, it is the board not being held in download mode.

Two things fix this in almost every case. The first is making sure nothing else owns the COM port. Arduino IDE, PuTTY, a serial monitor, a vendor tool, even a second browser tab with the flasher page open will inject exactly this kind of noise. Close all of them, unplug the miner, plug it back in, and open the flasher page in a fresh Chrome or Edge window (Firefox and Safari do not do Web Serial at all).

The second is forcing download mode by hand, which is where the button confusion bites. On the ESP32-S3 module there are two tiny tactile buttons, usually marked BOOT (or IO0) and RST (or EN). If yours are unlabeled, you can tell them apart by behaviour: press one on its own while the miner is running and watch the screen. The one that makes the unit restart is RESET, the other one is BOOT. Once you know which is which, do this with the USB cable already plugged in: press and hold BOOT, tap RESET once while still holding BOOT, wait about a second, then release BOOT. Windows should make the device connect sound again and the port will reappear, often under a slightly different name. Only then click Connect miner, pick the port, and hit Erase and install. If you get the same 0x45, you most likely had the buttons the other way round, so swap which one you hold and which one you tap and try once more.

One more thing worth checking: plug straight into a USB port on the PC, not a hub, a monitor or a dock. Hubs are a very common cause of the stub dying right after it loads, because the baud rate change does not survive them. And if your BC04 has two USB connectors on the controller board, use the one on the ESP32 module itself rather than the one on the mainboard.

Since you already have Harlo OS on the way in rather than installed, stick with the factory image and Erase and install for now. The O. image is only for units already running Harlo OS. Once it boots you will need to redo Wi-Fi and your pool settings, since a factory install wipes those.

If all of that still ends at 0x45, the fastest help on the planet for this is our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, where you can ping @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead). Post the full installation log there and he will spot it quickly. Send me the new log too if you prefer to keep it here, especially the last ten lines after you try the BOOT and RESET sequence, and I will take it from there.

Best,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Handed to the team · Web flasher stub fails on this unit; needs JD to confirm BC04 factory image offs

Hi there,

That second log actually answers the button question for you, so stop fighting the buttons. Look at the first line: VendorID 0x303a, ProductID 0x1001. That is Espressif's own USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral, which means your BC04 controller has no separate USB to serial bridge chip. The U. cable goes straight into the ESP32-S3 itself. On a board like that the chip is already answering from ROM when esptool sees it, which is why it reads the chip revision, the PSRAM and the MAC perfectly every single time. There is nothing wrong with your BOOT and RST technique, and no, you would not hear a different Windows sound or see a different device, because the port keeps the same identity in both modes. You have been chasing a problem that was never there.

The real failure is one line further down. Your log goes "Uploading stub... Running stub..." and then straight to the hard reset. The line that should sit between them, "Stub running.", never appears. The stub is a small helper program esptool loads into RAM to flash faster. On native USB boards the stub restarts the USB device when it starts, the browser loses the port it was holding, and the next thing esptool reads is the chip's own boot banner "ESP-ROM:esp32s3...", whose first byte is 0x45, the letter E. That is your error. It is a known rough edge of browser flashing on native USB ESP32-S3 boards, not a dead miner and not a bad cable.

The way around it is to flash without the stub, which the web flasher cannot do but the command line tool can. On one of your Windows machines install Python from python.org, ticking "Add python.exe to PATH" during setup, then open Command Prompt and run: pip install esptool. Next, go back to the Harlo firmware page and use the Download factory image link for HAMMER BC04 so you have the .bin file locally, and put it somewhere easy like C:\harlo. Find the COM port in Device Manager under Ports, it will show up as a USB Serial Device while the miner is plugged in.

Then run this, replacing COM5 with your port and the filename with the one you downloaded:

python -m esptool --chip esp32s3 --port COM5 --baud 115200 --no-stub write-flash 0x0 C:\harlo\hammer-bc04-factory.bin

The --no-stub part is the whole point, and 115200 keeps it slow and safe. Without the stub there is no compression, so expect it to take two or three minutes rather than fifteen seconds, and the progress percentage will crawl. That is normal, let it finish. If it complains the port is busy, close every browser tab with the flasher open, plus Arduino IDE or any serial monitor, and plug straight into a USB port on the machine rather than a hub, dock or monitor. If it still stalls at the connecting stage, hold BOOT while you plug the cable in, then release it and run the command again. When it ends with "Hash of data verified", unplug the miner from power for ten seconds and power it back up, and Harlo OS should come up with its own Wi-Fi setup access point.

One caveat I want to be straight about: the factory image for the BC04 should go at offset 0x0, but if the download page or the file name states a different offset, use that one instead of 0x0. I have asked JD, our hardware lead, to confirm the offset and whether this board batch needs the no-stub route as standard. The team is offline for the weekend and picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and their answer will come to you by email. If you would rather not wait, the fastest route by far is our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, where you can ping @nullhashrate, who is JD. Paste the command output there and he will have you sorted quickly.

Send me the output either way and I will keep going with you on it.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
